doc.title: Nancy Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995

title: Never nervous on stage
summary: She was always comfortable before an audience and needs to go home to replenish.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: Can you recall as a child, were you always pretty comfortable in front of an audience?
Always. I didn’t know you were supposed to be nervous.
It didn’t even occur to you.

It never occurred to me that you should be nervous. When I found out I was so grown that it didn’t make any difference. Then I found out people actually get nauseous and tremble and shake. Well I don’t want to do this if I have to be sick before I go on.
Why would I subject myself to that.

But some people do. Some people just feel that that’s a part of it. I like being relaxed. I like taking it in stride. I love it. I keep it in its proper perspective, and it allows me to continue to do it. As long as I do it this way I can do it. As long as I’m able to do it for a little while and go home and get what I need to give you. Because being out here doesn’t replenish. I have to go home for that. To be fulfilled, I need to go home in order to sing for you. I have to have that sense of well being and balance.
